body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SLO alert - production latency spike detected on inference pool us-west-2. p95 jumped from ~420ms to ~2.3s, p99 from ~1.1s to ~6.7s over the last 5m. Streaming stalls increased x5. Error rate (stream timeouts) up from 0.02% to 0.3%. Auto-investigation: KV cache eviction rate up 8x; slab fragmentation high; prefill queue depth increased vs decode worker throughput.

Olivia Chen: I'm on it. Checking routing + cache metrics. Notifying oncall to coordinate. @Samir @Jia please chime in if you see obvious quick mitigations.

Samir Patel: seeing same in dashboards. MapReduce: most of the affected requests are long-context streaming sessions hitting the kv-prefill codepath. Prefill latency exploded. Looks like prefill producers are queuing because decode workers are busy (decode <-> prefill imbalance).

Jia Park: can we confirm eviction pattern? pulling kv metrics now.

Jia Park: snippets from the memprof API:
```
kv.evictions_per_min: 480 -> 3900
kv.prefill_queue_len: 120 -> 950
kv.decode_workers_busy_pct: 92%
slab.fragmentation_ratio: 0.72
```
Prefill is backing up, causing hot keys to be evicted while prefill hasn't finished updating them -> increased cache churn.

Olivia Chen: probable root: fragmentation + sudden traffic spike of long sessions (customer A and background sampling) leading to frequent full-slab evictions. When slabs reshuffle, streaming tail requests hit cache misses and stall while waiting for prefill to complete.

Samir Patel: immediate mitigations I can do now: 1) route a fraction of traffic to smaller-context model variant (lower memory KV footprints) 2) temporarily increase per-shard kv-cache-size by toggling `kv.cache.reserve_pct` to 120% for us-west-2 to delay evictions 3) throttle prefill producers to avoid overwhelming decode workers. Which should I do first?

Olivia Chen: do (2) and (1) in parallel. (3) requires careful testing; do it if (2) doesn't stabilize. Also add a canary route to dedicated pool so critical customers aren't impacted.

Samir Patel: executing now - running rollout command to bump reserve_pct and add route:
```
# bump reserve on pool us-west-2
infractl kv-config set --pool us-west-2 --reserve-pct 120 --reason "live mitigation - evictions spike"
# route 10% traffic to variant-redwood-smaller
infractl route update --pool us-west-2 --model redwood/v1-small --pct 10 --reason "reduce kv footprint"
```
ETA 45s for config propagation.

Mike O'Leary: I'm taking the night handoff in ~20m; if this crosses into my shift I'll own follow-ups. Leave notes for postmortem.

Jia Park: watch the prefill vs decode ratio after reserve bump. Also enabling an experimental slab-compact toggle on one shard to test fragmentation rebuild (one shard first):
```
infractl kv-shard compact --shard id=usw2-12 --dry-run=false
```
This will temporarily increase CPU but should reduce fragmentation.

Luis Gomez: flagging customer-impact: streaming SDK sessions for customer `acme-marketing` show partial streaming with stalls at ~12:12 UTC. CS ticket already opened. @Olivia please coordinate comms if customer-visible regression persists.

Olivia Chen: noted. CS: prioritize Acme and one other high-traffic account. No evidence of data loss, only increased latency and partial streams.

incident-bot: Mitigation action recorded: reserve_pct bump + 10% reroute to redwood/v1-small + slab compact on shard usw2-12. Incident severity set to SEV2.

Samir Patel: reserve change is live. Early signals: p95 dropped from 2.3s -> 1.1s within 3 minutes, p99 still high ~3.9s. Evictions/sec trending down from 3.9k -> ~1.1k. Prefill queue depth falling slowly (950 -> 420).

Jia Park: slab compact completed on shard usw2-12. Fragmentation ratio on that shard down 0.72 -> 0.35. Good sign.

Olivia Chen: good. Next steps: keep reserve bump for 2 hours and monitor. If p99 not under SLO, do controlled throttle of prefill producers (reduce prefill concurrency by 30%) to avoid prefill decode imbalance.

Samir Patel: preparing prefill throttle patch rollout to one shard:
```
# reduce prefill workers
infractl config set --service prefill --concurrency 70% --scope shard:usw2-*
```
Planning to roll to 20% of shards first.

Mike O'Leary: handoff note: when I take over I'll keep the reserve_pct bump and compact status in the incident doc, and if we still see >x2 p99 I'll promote to emergency scaling (burst extra cache nodes).

Olivia Chen: monitoring for customer impact. @Luis please provide a short CS update: "We’re seeing intermittent streaming slowdowns in us-west-2, mitigation in progress. No data loss. Services are gradually returning to normal."

Luis Gomez: ack, sending now.

Samir Patel: rolled prefill throttle to 20% shards; immediate improvement in prefill queue: 420 -> 280; decode worker busy -> 68%. p99 down to 2.0s.

Olivia Chen: can we confirm streaming stall counts down?

Jia Park: yes. streaming.stalls/5m: 120 -> 24. Looks stable.

incident-bot: Incident update: p95=680ms, p99=1.9s, streaming stalls down 80%. Continue monitoring.

Olivia Chen: I'll leave this open for one more hour to ensure stability then start a postmortem. Key hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation + sudden long-session traffic led to prefill vs decode worker imbalance and cascading evictions. Mitigations that helped: increased kv.reserve_pct, slab compact on hot shard, throttle prefill producers, traffic reroute to smaller model variant.

Jia Park: logging action items for postmortem: 1) add automatic slab defrag heuristics 2) tune prefill/decode backpressure 3) add early-detection alert for prefill queue growth and eviction spikes 4) revisit default per-shard reserve_pct.

Mike O'Leary: taking handoff now. Current state: p95=640ms p99=1.6s streaming_stalls~18/5m. Keeping reserve bump and throttles. Will escalate to burst cache nodes if p99 rises.

Olivia Chen: thanks Mike. Closing timeline note: first alert 1701234567, mitigations applied within 12 minutes, major stabilizations within 35 minutes. Will draft PM and include customer-impact timeline.

Samir Patel: adding logs we used for debugging (paste):
```
# find hot keys
kubectl logs -l app=kv-monitor -c profiler --since=10m | jq '.hot_keys | sort_by(.evictions) | reverse | .[:10]'
# prefill queue sample
curl -s "https://metrics.internal/kv/prefill?pool=us-west-2" | jq '.queues | {avg_len,95p,99p}'
```
Keep these for the postmortem.

Luis Gomez: CS updated customers at 12:20 UTC and again at 12:40 UTC. No escalations yet.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident is now in steady state. Leave open for postmortem.

Mike O'Leary: closing oncall handoff notes: follow-up owners - Samir (prefill/decode tuning), Jia (kv fragmentation fixes), Olivia (postmortem + customer comms).

Olivia Chen: thanks team. I'll create the postmortem and link this thread.

Samir Patel: quick note for runbook: add temporary knob `kv.cache.reserve_pct` as a recommended mitigation for eviction storms.

Jia Park: and add a rollout test for slab-compact on staging so we can eyeball CPU impact.

Luis Gomez: will monitor CS tickets overnight. Ping me if anything flares.

Olivia Chen: good work everyone.
